agent.name: Organizational Adoption of Emerging Technologies Agent
agent.specialty: Organizational readiness, absorption, governance, and sustainability

analytical_question: Can this hospital absorb, govern and sustain a bounded Mako-assisted elective TKR evaluation independently of whether the technology has established clinical/economic value?
general_et_finding: Mako is an established surgeon-controlled orthopaedic robotic-assistance platform requiring patient-specific CT planning; NHS use is conditionally supported within NICE evidence generation rather than unconditional routine-use endorsement. Organizational differences do not change these external facts.
application_finding: For elective primary TKR in advanced knee osteoarthritis, alignment/planning precision is not itself proof of faster functional recovery. The 2026 RACER-Knee randomized trial found no clinically meaningful 12-month patient benefit and greater cost than conventional TKR; the application comparative value remains conditional and needs locally justified evidence generation, not benefit claims based on robotics generally.

evidence.claim: NICE permits Mako and selected robotic-assisted systems for hip/knee replacements during evidence generation with specified conditions.
evidence.notes: Guidance does not establish a specific hospital's permissions.

evidence.claim: Service adoption needs planned workforce, procurement, training and clinical governance arrangements.
evidence.source_or_reference: NHS England/GIRFT robotic-assisted surgery implementation guide (2025)
evidence.notes: Specific local closure evidence still required.

evidence.claim: Robotic-assisted knee replacement did not establish clinically important 12-month outcome advantage at a higher cost.
evidence.source_or_reference: Parsons et al., RACER-Knee randomized trial, The Lancet (2026)
evidence.notes: External application-level counterevidence, constant across hospitals.

evidence.claim: Hospital staffing, infrastructure, training and budget details are hypothetical assessment inputs.
evidence.notes: Do not mistake these for validated real hospital records.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: RACER-Knee supplies contrary outcome/economic evidence: clinical benefit and cost-effectiveness must not be presumed.
Hospital cases are hypothetical; no local staff training records, signed committee approval, funded service plan or service contract was examined.
External guidance is not proof of local compliance.
value_opportunity_implication: A justified bounded evaluation could produce local safety, functional outcome and whole-life cost evidence, but improved recovery cannot be assumed.
risk_governance_implication: Patient harm, inappropriate consent, CT/data workflow failure and unavailable equipment are unacceptable clinical risks until governance, competence, fallback and ownership are verified.
change_monitoring_triggers: At day 90, review documented safety gates, named owners, competency completion and fully funded operating plan before revisiting the verdict.
Reconsider when new NICE guidance or high-quality comparative knee recovery and cost evidence becomes available.
Suspend/withhold patient use if clinical incidents, missing service support or incomplete audit records arise.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Request signed Mako-specific surgeon and theatre-team competencies plus proctor plan from clinical education lead: without them do not authorize patient procedures.
Request governance approval, consent and fallback protocol from hospital clinical governance lead: no live-patient decision without these.
Request whole-life budget, case-volume, maintenance contract and ongoing operational owner from finance/procurement/operations: cannot conclude sustainable adoption.
organization_specific_finding: Application fit: CONDITIONAL/UNPROVEN BETTER PATIENT RECOVERY. Organizational readiness: EXECUTIVE SUPPORT DOES NOT MAKE A 30-DAY LIVE LAUNCH SAFE; BLOCK. Dimensions: 1. leadership/sponsorship=3 [CASE ASSUMPTION committed sponsor]; 2. skills/training=U [MISSING EVIDENCE Mako competencies/proctoring]; 3. workflow/process=1 [CASE ASSUMPTION no tested fallback]; 4. infrastructure/data=2 [CASE ASSUMPTION on-site CT but interface unverified]; 5. resources/budget=2 [CASE ASSUMPTION capital exists; recurring spend U]; 6. governance/risk=0 [CASE ASSUMPTION local committee has not authorized]; 7. culture/change=2 [CASE ASSUMPTION leading-edge appetite; staff burden not tested]; 8. operating ownership=U [MISSING EVIDENCE patient audit owner and vendor SLA]. Strengths: senior support; available capital and CT. Gaps: clinical approval is absent; training and contingency not verified. Highest-consequence gap: no signed governance authorization and competency evidence despite accelerated rollout.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High that the hypothetical 30-day go-live is blocked by explicit missing approval; low about real trust-specific execution. Executive urgency cannot remove safety requirements.
recommendation_management_implication: 1) BLOCK proposed 30-day clinical launch. Proposed medical director/clinical governance chair (VERIFY) must provide explicit approval and NICE conditions before any patient procedure. 2) Proposed surgeon education and theatre leads (VERIFY) complete and document robotic proficiency, proctorship, CT workflow and fallback simulation. 3) Proposed finance/operations leads (VERIFY) sign the vendor SLA, whole-life service plan and data/audit ownership. 4) Review at day 90 or when gates are closed; only consider bounded evidence generation if clinical/economic value independently justifies it.
